title: Cellar and Winter
premise: Juniper Sterling takes a teaching post in the dying town of Harrow's Bend, where eleven students vanished between 1962 and 1974 and no one will say why. Her rented farmhouse belonged to Ellery Voss, the school custodian who disappeared in 1974, and its cellar holds a ledger of names written in a child's hand—names that begin appearing in her own class roster. The house's mirrors lag one second behind reality because something in the walls is still catching up to what happened there. Juniper learns the missing children were taken as payment for a bargain the town's founders made with whatever lives beneath the school, and that the debt renews every harvest moon unless it is returned. In the end she cannot save everyone: she carries the ledger into the cellar during the moonrise and gives back the one thing that was truly stolen—the town's memory of its own guilt—and walks out as the mirrors finally show her in real time, while Harrow's Bend forgets she was ever there.
about_author: Felix Sandoval is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in towns too small to appear on maps before turning to writing full-time. He collects local histories and insists that every ghost story is really a court transcript no one filed.

chapters.title: The Long Drive In
chapters.summary: Juniper arrives in Harrow's Bend at dusk, counting roadkill and empty storefronts, and signs the lease on the Voss farmhouse from a landlord who won't step past the porch. POV: Juniper. Beat: wary hope, the first note of wrongness when the landlord calls the cellar 'settled.'

chapters.title: Eleven Empty Desks
chapters.summary: On her first day teaching eighth grade, Juniper finds the yearbook wall with eleven photos removed and a janitor's closet nobody has keys for. A student, Marisol, whispers that the school 'eats slow.' POV: Juniper. Beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Juniper begins her notebook: dates, overheard remarks, the exact wording of evasions from Principal Grieves. She photographs the sealed cellar door at school. POV: Juniper. Beat: control through ritual; the reader sees obsession forming.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: At home, Juniper notices her reflection blinks after she does. She tests it with a metronome and confirms the mirror lags exactly one second. POV: Juniper. Beat: quiet dread; the horror becomes domestic.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows the Names
chapters.summary: Marisol recites the eleven missing students' names like a nursery rhyme but can't say where she learned them. Juniper cross-references: all vanished in harvest season. POV: Juniper with a Marisol interlude. Beat: tenderness toward the child, alarm at what she carries.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Cellar Floor
chapters.summary: Following a draft smell, Juniper pries up a floorboard and finds Ellery Voss's ledger—a child's handwriting listing names, dates, and payments rendered. The last entry is 1974, unfinished. POV: Juniper. Beat: discovery; the inheritance theme turns literal.

chapters.title: Grieves Denies Everything Politely
chapters.summary: Juniper confronts the principal with the ledger; he offers her a raise and a different house. His hands shake as he pours coffee neither drinks. POV: Juniper. Beat: institutional gaslighting; justice outside the law begins to feel necessary.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Shows Instead
chapters.summary: The lagging reflection starts showing the room as it looked decades ago—a child's bed, chalk dust, a small coat on a hook. Juniper realizes the mirror remembers. POV: Juniper. Beat: awe braided with terror; memory made architectural.

chapters.title: Ellery Voss, Custodian
chapters.summary: At the county archive, Juniper reads Voss's file: hired 1961, praised, then increasingly erratic complaints about 'the arrangement' before his 1974 disappearance. A photo shows him holding the ledger. POV: Juniper. Beat: grief for a stranger; the predecessor's ghost becomes a companion.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival Preparations
chapters.summary: The town buzzes with festival planning; every adult deflects Juniper's questions with cheerful menace. A farmer tells her the moon this year is 'a big one.' POV: Juniper. Beat: claustrophobic social horror; the countdown begins.

chapters.title: Marisol's Name Appears
chapters.summary: A twelfth name surfaces in the ledger in fresh ink: Marisol Quintero. Juniper scrubs at it; the ink returns by morning. POV: Juniper. Beat: stakes become personal; protective fury ignites.

chapters.title: The Second Reflection
chapters.summary: Juniper's mirror now shows a second figure standing behind her delayed image—small, patient. It doesn't appear when she turns around. POV: Juniper. Beat: escalation; she stops sleeping with lights off.

chapters.title: Records Burn Better Than Questions
chapters.summary: The county archive burns overnight. Juniper's photocopies survive in her car; she understands someone is watching her documentation. POV: Juniper. Beat: paranoia justified; the enemy is organized.

chapters.title: Doraleen Hask, Class of 1973
chapters.summary: Juniper finds one survivor of the missing years living outside town. Doraleen, ancient and sharp, says only: 'We paid so the rest could eat. You want to take that back?' POV: Doraleen. Beat: moral complication—the town's complicity has beneficiaries.

chapters.title: The Bargain of the Founders
chapters.summary: Doraleen explains: in 1931 the founders traded a child every few harvests to the thing under the school in exchange for the valley never flooding. The ledger records the debts. Voss tried to end it. POV: Doraleen. Beat: the full mythos lands; justice vs. survival framed.

chapters.title: Voss's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Deciphering faded pages, Juniper finds Voss's plan: return what was taken—not a new payment, but restitution—to break the contract. He failed because he went alone, at the wrong hour. POV: Juniper. Beat: a plan forms; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Parent-Teacher Night
chapters.summary: Every parent attends except Marisol's, who sends an aunt who stares at Juniper's notebook and says, 'Stop writing.' That night the notebook's pages are blank. POV: Juniper. Beat: violation; her prayer has been answered by something else.

chapters.title: She Rewrites It From Memory
chapters.summary: Juniper reconstructs the notebook from memory, hand cramping, refusing to stop. The mirror shows the small figure applauding slowly. POV: Juniper. Beat: defiance; documentation as resistance.

chapters.title: The School After Hours
chapters.summary: Juniper breaks into the sealed wing and finds the janitor's closet open onto stairs going down further than the building is tall. Chalk lines mark tally marks—hundreds. POV: Juniper. Beat: threshold crossed; no retreat psychologically.

chapters.title: Tally Marks and Small Shoes
chapters.summary: In the deep corridor she finds shoes arranged in pairs, sized for children across five decades, and hears humming that matches the tune Marisol sang. She flees as the humming follows. POV: Juniper. Beat: visceral terror; the cost made physical.

chapters.title: Grieves Breaks
chapters.summary: Cornered with evidence, Grieves confesses his family has been 'bookkeepers' since 1931—he doesn't choose the names, the ledger does. He begs her to let Marisol go through with it quietly. POV: Grieves. Beat: the banality of evil weeping; no ally here.

chapters.title: Marisol Runs Away
chapters.summary: Marisol, sensing she's chosen, disappears. Juniper searches the fields all night while the town pointedly does not help. POV: Juniper. Beat: desperation; the clock is now days, not weeks.

chapters.title: Found in the Flood Plain
chapters.summary: Juniper finds Marisol asleep in the dry riverbed, drawn there, she says, by the humming. The ground beneath them is warm. POV: Juniper. Beat: relief shadowed by certainty—the thing is already reaching for her.

chapters.title: Doraleen's Price
chapters.summary: Doraleen agrees to help perform Voss's rite but demands inclusion: her brother was taken in 1968 and she wants to see him returned or avenged. POV: Doraleen. Beat: alliance forged from grief; the team of three unlikely witnesses.

chapters.title: Reading the Contract
chapters.summary: Studying the ledger's margins, they learn the entity's terms: it keeps what is freely given, but stolen things must be returned if named correctly at the hour of the moon. The children were not given—they were taken by the founders. POV: Juniper. Beat: legalistic horror; a loophole is the whole plot.

chapters.title: The Town Notices Her
chapters.summary: Juniper's tires are slashed, her classroom ransacked, and a note in old-fashioned script says STAY INVISIBLE. She posts copies of the ledger to three out-of-state addresses. POV: Juniper. Beat: isolation weaponized; insurance against the ending.

chapters.title: The Mirrors All Lag Now
chapters.summary: Every reflective surface in town—windows, spoons, eyes—is one second late. The whole town is being watched by its own past. POV: Juniper observing others. Beat: scale shift; private haunting becomes communal.

chapters.title: Voss's Remains
chapters.summary: Behind the cellar wall, Juniper finds Voss's skeleton seated, ledger page in hand, having died mid-rite in 1974. Clutched in his other hand: the correct name of the first stolen child. POV: Juniper. Beat: sorrowful resolve; she finishes another person's sentence.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: The three rehearse the rite: name each stolen child aloud, return the ledger, refuse to offer anything new. Doraleen warns that the thing will offer bargains, and it lies beautifully. POV: Doraleen. Beat: calm before catastrophe; love expressed as preparation.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises Early
chapters.summary: Cloud cover parts a day ahead of schedule—the thing controls the calendar now. They have hours, not days. Marisol's name in the ledger darkens to black. POV: Juniper. Beat: panic; the trap springs.

chapters.title: Grieves Locks the Doors
chapters.summary: Grieves, terrified of flood and ruin, seals the school and takes Marisol to deliver her himself. Juniper and Doraleen chase him through the building as the humming swells. POV: alternating. Beat: betrayal climax; man as the monster's hand.

chapters.title: Down the Long Stairs
chapters.summary: They descend past the shoes into a chamber that is the cellar, the school, and the flooded valley of 1931 all at once. The founders' ghosts stand in a ring, still signing. POV: Juniper. Beat: surreal apex; the past is a place you can stand in.

chapters.title: The Bargain Offered
chapters.summary: The entity appears as every missing child at once, then as everything each of them has lost, offering Marisol's safety for the ledger back and silence forever. Doraleen nearly says yes. POV: Juniper. Beat: temptation scene; the lie is beautiful.

chapters.title: Naming the Stolen
chapters.summary: Juniper reads all eleven names plus Voss's own, declaring each one stolen, not given, demanding return per the terms. The chamber floods with cold light; the founders' signatures burn off the air. POV: Juniper. Beat: climax; the courtroom is her voice.

chapters.title: What Comes Back Isn't Right
chapters.summary: Something answers—but it returns the children as the moment of their taking, screaming, and the chamber begins collapsing. Doraleen steps forward to receive her brother and does not come back out. POV: Juniper. Beat: victory with amputation; justice costs.

chapters.title: Carrying Them Up
chapters.summary: Juniper drags Marisol and two returned children—now aged as they would have been, dazed—up the stairs as the school groans. Grieves stands aside, weeping, and holds the door. POV: Juniper. Beat: endurance; the banal man's single act of grace.

chapters.title: Moonset
chapters.summary: As the moon sets, the mirrors snap into real time. The remaining founders' descendants wander the streets unable to remember why they're relieved. The river runs high and harmless. POV: Juniper. Beat: eerie peace; the debt dissolved by truth.

chapters.title: The Town Forgets Her
chapters.summary: No record of Juniper Sterling exists in Harrow's Bend—her contract, her photos, her mailbox, gone. Only Marisol and the returned remember her. POV: Marisol. Beat: bittersweet erasure; the price of breaking contracts is standing outside history.

chapters.title: The New Teacher's Notebook
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a new teacher moves into the farmhouse and finds a notebook hidden in the floorboards, addressed 'To whoever documents next.' The last mirror in the house reflects perfectly. POV: the new teacher. Beat: cyclical chill softened into guardianship.

chapters.title: Cellar and Winter
chapters.summary: Juniper, teaching in another state, receives a letter in a child's hand: 'We remember you. The cellar is just a cellar now.' She writes back and files the letter in a box labeled EVIDENCE OF GOOD. POV: Juniper. Beat: resolution; memory kept deliberately, justice done without law, winter survived.
